title: A WebSocket reconnect attempt that cannot connect kills the bot: no socket has an error listener, so the ws library throws its error event as an uncaught exception and the process exits

evidence.note: the try around new WebSocketProvider only catches synchronous throws; the doc comment at :834 says the constructor "raises if RPC unreachable; loops", which is not what the library does
the constructor calls new WebSocket(url) and sets only onopen and onmessage; no onerror, so a failed connect is not caught by the constructor and no error listener exists

a refused connect or an unexpected upgrade response (for example HTTP 429) calls emitErrorAndClose / abortHandshake, which does websocket.emit('error', err); receiverOnError (:1176-1192) does the same for a bad frame on a live socket
no output: no error listener on any socket and no uncaughtException handler anywhere in src

evidence.ref: node -e "const {WebSocketProvider}=require('ethers');const p=new WebSocketProvider('ws://127.0.0.1:1',1);p.websocket.on('close',...)" (Node 22.16.0, loopback only, no src import)
evidence.note: printed "constructed without throw", then "Unhandled 'error' event ... connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:1 ... at emitErrorAndClose (ws/lib/websocket.js:1035)", exit=1; the same script with an error listener printed "error handled: ECONNREFUSED", "close handler ran", "still alive after 3s", exit=0
the RECONNECT_FAILURE_ALERT tier and the backoff growth live in the catch; the >60 s tier (:889-914) needs a later loop pass; a refused connect ends the process before either is reached
V3 DEX reconnect builds a provider the same way (no error listener)
getWsProvider at boot and in onRestart (bot.ts:1815), same

sibling_sites_checked: Every WebSocketProvider construction at the base: detector.ts:921, bot.ts:1561, bot.ts:1603, provider.ts:37 (git grep). None attaches an error listener. Once a connection is established, a socket-level error (ECONNRESET) is handled inside ws by socketOnError (websocket.js:1328-1338), which destroys the socket without emitting error on the WebSocket, so a plain drop only closes; a protocol error on a live socket (receiverOnError) does emit error and crashes the same way. AUD-BUY-005 (no unhandledRejection handler) is the promise-rejection sibling; this is a synchronous EventEmitter throw, a separate mechanism with the same effect.
severity_rationale: S1. Effect: the process exits, so every open position on every chain loses its exit monitor and anti-rug protection until the operator restarts the bot (there is no supervisor). Condition: the endpoint is unreachable or refuses the upgrade (outage, 429, 5xx, DNS) at the moment of a reconnect attempt, 1 s after any socket drop; plausible, because drops often come from the same provider trouble. Not S0: a drop followed by a successful reconnect does not crash.
recommendation: Attach an error listener to every WebSocket before it can fail (part of the single WebSocket owner, card OD-11); treat a failed connect as a failed attempt that stays in the backoff loop, so the tiered alerts become reachable; decide the process-level uncaught-exception policy together with AUD-BUY-005. Phase 24, proven in Phase 23 with a refused-connect test against a real socket (not a mocked provider).
